beats.say: The CEO's sales dashboard takes 40 seconds to load.
And it shows yesterday's numbers.
beats.label: It gets worse
beats.head: And the numbers are a day old

beats.say: Fix three things: the speed, the freshness, and who can see what.
beats.label: Station 4.1 · Data for visualization

beats.say: First: which tool shows the data?
Looker Studio is free and quick. Great for simple dashboards.
beats.label: Quick dashboards
beats.head: Looker Studio

beats.say: Looker adds a shared dictionary of metrics, so revenue means one thing for everyone.
beats.label: Governed metrics
beats.head: Looker

beats.say: Connected Sheets lets spreadsheet people work on billions of rows, without an export.
beats.label: Spreadsheet people
beats.head: Connected Sheets

beats.say: And BI Engine keeps data in memory, so dashboards answer in under a second.
beats.label: Speed
beats.head: BI Engine: in-memory, sub-second

beats.say: One classic trap. Looker Studio shows old data? It is the cache. Change the data freshness setting.
beats.label: Exam trap
beats.text: Old data in Looker Studio: change data freshness.

check.prompt: A dashboard runs the same heavy total all day. What helps most?
check.why: A materialized view stores the answer and keeps it fresh.

beats.say: Second: stop doing the same work again and again.
A dashboard asks the same question all day. So work out the answer once.
beats.label: The idea
beats.head: Answer once, serve many times

beats.say: Use a materialized view, a scheduled summary table, or BI Engine.
beats.label: Three ways

beats.say: And the same query, asked twice, is served from the cache, free, for about 24 hours.

check.prompt: Does LIMIT 10 reduce the bytes that an on-demand query scans?
check.why: BigQuery still scans every byte of the columns. LIMIT only cuts the rows it returns.

beats.say: Third: one query is still slow. Now what?
Do not guess. Open the query plan. It shows bytes, slot time, and skew.
beats.label: Step one
beats.head: Read the query plan

beats.say: Almost every fix is one of two things. Scan less, or shuffle less.
beats.label: The two fixes
beats.head: Scan less. Shuffle less.

beats.say: Select only the columns you need. Filter on the partition early. And cut data down before a join.
beats.label: In practice

beats.say: The trap: adding LIMIT to save money. BigQuery still scans every byte.
beats.label: Exam trap
beats.text: LIMIT does not reduce the bytes scanned.

beats.say: Last: who can see what on the dashboard?
Give viewers a view, or a curated dataset. Never the raw tables.
beats.label: The rule
beats.head: Views, not raw tables

beats.say: And mask sensitive columns with policy tags. Share with groups, not people.
beats.label: Inside a table
beats.head: Mask columns. Share with groups.

beats.say: Recap.
Pick the BI tool for the audience. Compute once, and read many times.
beats.label: Station 4.1 · 1 of 2

beats.say: Read the plan, then scan less. And give viewers views, not raw tables.
beats.label: Station 4.1 · 2 of 2
